core.purpose: Establish the system-wide engineering foundation and clean architecture boundaries.
invariants: Domain rules remain independent from delivery/runtime vendors.
Every authoritative datum has an explicit owner and source of truth.
All production changes are observable, testable, reversible, and evidence-linked.
No adapter or framework may become the canonical business model.
security: Deny by default at trust boundaries.
Secrets never enter source control or logs.
Dependency and supply-chain checks are mandatory.
operations: Structured logging, metrics, tracing where useful.
Runbooks for failure, rollback, restore, and incident response.
recovery: Authoritative data is backed up and restore-tested.
Changes define rollback or forward-recovery before release.

invariants: Server-side authorization remains authoritative.
UI state never becomes the source of truth.
Critical actions expose clear confirmation/recovery states.
Accessibility is native, not retrofit.
operations: Performance budgets and real-user signals where applicable.
recovery: No irreversible client migration without server compatibility.

mobile.purpose: Mobile application surface with device-aware safety.
invariants: Server remains authoritative unless an explicit offline model is selected.
Local data is minimized and encrypted when sensitive.
Device lifecycle and revocation are explicit.
security: Certificate/network protections appropriate to threat model.
No secrets embedded in application bundles.
tests: Offline/sync tests only when offline capability is selected.

invariants: Local state is explicit and bounded.
Business truth is not silently forked onto unmanaged clients.
recovery: Local data export/recovery if authoritative local state exists.

invariants: Contracts are versioned and compatibility-managed.
Writes are idempotent where retries are possible.
Authorization is enforced on every protected resource.
security: Authentication, authorization, rate limiting, input validation.

invariants: Destructive commands are explicit and fail closed.
Exit codes and output contracts are stable for automation.

identity.purpose: Identity, authentication, session, and role boundary.
invariants: Identity proof, authentication, authorization, and entitlement are separate concerns.
Sessions and credentials have explicit lifecycle and revocation.
Least privilege is default.
operations: Auth failure/anomaly monitoring without secret leakage.

invariants: Tenant context is explicit and immutable within a request/transaction.
Cross-tenant access is deny-by-default.
Sharing/collaboration is explicit, scoped, and audited.
security: Tenant-scoped authorization on every owned object.
No tenant identifier may be trusted solely from client input.
operations: Tenant dimension in audit/observability without leaking sensitive data.
recovery: Cross-tenant repair requires elevated authority and audit.

invariants: Every aggregate/entity has explicit ownership and lifecycle.
Business invariants are enforced close to domain truth.
Vendor/framework semantics do not leak into the domain.
security: Sensitive domain attributes are classified and access-scoped.
tests: Property tests for critical calculations where useful.
recovery: Migrations protect semantic meaning, not only columns.

workflow.purpose: Workflow, approval, task, and state-transition orchestration.
invariants: State transitions are explicit and validated.
Approval identity/time/reason are auditable.
Duplicate delivery cannot cause duplicate business effects.
security: Authorization is checked per transition, not only per screen.
High-impact approvals enforce required authority/dual control.
recovery: Compensating transitions or explicit irreversible boundary.

invariants: Object metadata and ownership are explicit.
Storage objects are never authorized by opaque URL possession alone.
Integrity/lifecycle are managed.
security: Malware/content scanning when untrusted uploads exist.
operations: Storage growth, scan failures, orphan detection.
recovery: Object/version recovery and metadata consistency checks.

invariants: Search index is derived unless explicitly justified otherwise.
Index can be rebuilt from authoritative sources.
Authorization filtering cannot be bypassed by search.
security: Search results obey the same object authorization model.
operations: Index lag, failure, size, query latency.

analytics.purpose: Reporting, analytics, dashboard, and export capability.
invariants: Metric definitions are versioned and reproducible.
Analytics is not an accidental source of transactional truth.
Exports respect authorization and data minimization.
recovery: Rebuild derived aggregates from source data.

commercial.purpose: Commercial editions, subscriptions, entitlements, trials, and licensing.
invariants: Entitlement is separate from payment-provider state.
Commercial state transitions are explicit and auditable.
Product capability gates are centrally defined.
operations: Entitlement mismatch and lifecycle failure monitoring.
recovery: Provider outage does not silently corrupt entitlement truth.
Manual correction is audited and reversible.

payments.purpose: Payment, invoice, refund, tax, and reconciliation boundary.
invariants: Provider adapter isolates external payment semantics.
Every money-moving write is idempotent.
Ledger/reconciliation distinguishes requested, provider, and settled state.
security: Do not store raw payment credentials when a provider can tokenize.

invariants: Notification request and delivery state are separate.
Retry cannot duplicate consequential external effects.
User/channel preferences are explicit where required.
External semantics terminate at adapters.
Timeout/retry/circuit-breaker behavior is explicit.
Compatibility and version ownership are known.
operations: Per-provider health, latency, error, quota signals.

invariants: Local authoritative scope is explicitly defined.
Conflict resolution is deterministic.
Sync operations are idempotent and tenant-safe.

globalization.purpose: Localization, timezone, currency, and RTL capability.
invariants: Canonical data representation is locale-independent.
Presentation formatting is locale-aware.
Timezone meaning is explicit for scheduled/business events.
recovery: Data remains canonical when locale settings change.

invariants: AI output is not treated as verified fact without evidence.
Model/provider/version and input evidence are reproducible for consequential outputs.
Tool/action authority is explicit and risk-derived.
security: Tool permission boundary and secret isolation.
operations: Quality, cost, latency, refusal/failure, provider/model version signals.

migration.purpose: Legacy migration, coexistence, import/export, and transition architecture.
invariants: Source-to-target mapping is explicit.
Migration is measurable and reconcilable.
Cutover has rollback/forward-recovery criteria.
security: Migration credentials/data extracts are controlled and time-bounded.
recovery: Documented abort point and rollback/forward-fix path.

invariants: External users have an explicit trust boundary.
Public and authenticated content paths are separated.
Embedded/public capabilities never inherit internal privileges.
operations: External journey availability and abuse signals.
recovery: Safe session revocation and backward-compatible frontend rollout.

invariants: Obligations are evidence-backed and freshness-bounded.
Data minimization, purpose, retention, and access are explicit.
Compliance claims never exceed evidence.
security: Sensitive data has stronger access/audit controls as required.

reliability.purpose: High-impact reliability, availability, realtime, and assurance.
invariants: SLIs/SLOs reflect user/business outcomes.
Failure domains and blast radius are explicit.
High-impact changes require independent assurance.
security: Emergency access is controlled and audited.
tests: Human oversight tests for high-impact operations.
operations: Error budget, saturation, dependency health, recovery metrics.
recovery: Defined RTO/RPO derived from business impact evidence.

custom.purpose: Hold user-added requirements that do not yet have a deterministic capability mapping, without silently dropping or guessing them.
invariants: Every custom requirement is preserved verbatim with a stable ID.
Custom text never silently activates an implementation technology.
Architecture review must map each custom requirement to existing or newly approved capabilities before implementation.
security: Custom requirements are reviewed for new trust boundaries, sensitive data, authority, and abuse cases.
tests: Traceability test from custom requirement ID to final mapped capability/module.
Acceptance tests are added before implementation after mapping.
operations: Operational impact must be classified during architecture review.
recovery: No implementation begins until rollback/compensation implications are recorded.
